title: test: reproduce unsupported PCB bend centerlines
description: Reproduces unsupported-element diagnostics for two PCB bend elements that do not render centerlines in WebGPU.
body:
Two `pcb_bend` elements produce unsupported-element diagnostics and no centerlines in WebGPU. This records the problem before the implementation in #44, using horizontal and vertical bends on separate boards with nonzero centers.

The geometry test asserts both diagnostics. The visual test enables bend visibility and uses the existing `prepareComparison` and `featureSnapshot` helpers: circuit-to-svg on the left shows both lines and labels, while WebGPU on the right is missing them. Both panels use the same Circuit JSON and viewport.

This PR changes only the fixture, geometry test, visual test, and paired bend snapshot. It uses the normal `circuit-to-svg@0.0.451` dependency already on `main` after #45. Dependencies, CI workflows, and unrelated snapshots match `main`.

Stacked fix: #44 starts directly at this repro commit (`b9701ee`) and adds one fix commit (`5d629d5`). Review/merge this repro first; a maintainer can create the upstream repro branch and retarget #44. Until then, #44 targets `main` and includes this repro. This pair supersedes #42.

Validation: 87 unit tests; typecheck, build, and formatting; 24 visual checks including the side-by-side bend snapshot. GitHub renderer and parity-regression checks pass after rebasing onto `950fe13`: 597 feature snapshots pass with zero new regressions. The strict audit retains the same 400 SVG mismatches and 12 frozen-reference failures as `main`.

![Reproduction: circuit-to-svg left, WebGPU right](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anil08607/circuit-json-webgpu/b9701ee79088516e6ca243dbe38568eee296701c/tests/snapshots/features/pcb-bend.png)

title: fix: match Canvas behavior for PCB bends and stiffeners
description: Fixes repeated diagnostics for unsupported PCB elements by recognizing and skipping mechanical elements like pcb_bend and pcb_stiffener in the 2D view.
body:
PCBs containing `pcb_bend` or `pcb_stiffener` currently produce repeated “Unsupported PCB element” diagnostics in the WebGPU viewer. Recognize these mechanical elements and skip them in the flat 2D view, matching circuit-to-canvas. Other unknown PCB types still report diagnostics.

Regression coverage includes a bend, a rotated rectangular stiffener, and a polygon stiffener on both attachment faces. It checks empty standalone geometry, unchanged WebGPU paint/erase meshes and element-ID mappings, and unchanged Canvas pixels for top and bottom copper views against the frozen reference.

Validation: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (88 passing), `bun run build`, and `bun run format:check`.

title: Share the default stall model across compatible NEMA17 controllers
description: Uses the existing NEMA17 current-pattern model as a shared default across compatible DRV8825 controllers, removing hardcoded serial-number eligibility checks from estimator initialization and stall-based homing, allowing Gantry YY to home without a separate calibration run.
body:
Use the existing NEMA17 current-pattern model as a shared default across compatible DRV8825 controllers. Remove the hardcoded serial-number eligibility checks from estimator initialization and stall-based homing so Gantry YY can home without a separate calibration run.

Expose `current_stall_model_scope: shared-default` and identify the shared model in the UI without implying it was independently calibrated on every motor. Per-controller sensitivity and operating-range/freshness checks remain. Fix the firmware download page's accidentally substituted PCB version back to 1.0.42. Firmware is 1.0.17.

Validation: native suite including reinitialization and homing eligibility for XX, YY and a third controller ID; dashboard tests. Both controllers will be flashed and re-identified without initiating homing.

title: Add stall sensitivity and bounded single-axis/XY homing
description: Changes Add saved stall sensitivity and Run Stall-based Homing on the single-axis, XY, and general motor pages. The sensitivity slider moves the current-score threshold used by the graph, warning and homing detector. NEMA23 retains its torque-threshold control. Homing seeks both ends, verifies release during each backoff, applies a conservative contactdetector allowance, saves the usable travel range, and returns to zero. Each leg has a finite travel ceiling and timeout. Stop, USBheartbeat loss and faults abort. Two connected axes run sequentially, and a failed axis cancels the batch. The firmware reserves queued STEP pulses against the saved bounds, rejects out-of-range finite moves and clips joggingbraking at the boundary. Reboot preserves bounds but requires a fresh home; homing changes the coordinate session so old saved positions cannot be reused.  Validation Native tests: two-contact state machine, clear-stall requirement, no-contacttimeoutcancel paths, settings migrationpersistence, both travel bounds and queued-pulse reservations. Dashboard tests: sensitivity commands, singleXY homing, sequential execution, cancellation, connectionpower failures. Existing nativedashboard suites and 45 Python tests pass. Local ARM builds pass for all three board profiles. Physical end-stop homing has not been run: mechanism suitability is awaiting operator confirmation. These are inferred commanded-step bounds, not encoder-backed travel protection.
body:
## Changes
Add saved stall sensitivity and **Run Stall-based Homing** on the single-axis, XY, and general motor pages. The sensitivity slider moves the current-score threshold used by the graph, warning and homing detector. NEMA23 retains its torque-threshold control.

Homing seeks both ends, verifies release during each backoff, applies a conservative contact/detector allowance, saves the usable travel range, and returns to zero. Each leg has a finite travel ceiling and timeout. Stop, USB/heartbeat loss and faults abort. Two connected axes run sequentially, and a failed axis cancels the batch.

The firmware reserves queued STEP pulses against the saved bounds, rejects out-of-range finite moves and clips jogging/braking at the boundary. Reboot preserves bounds but requires a fresh home; homing changes the coordinate session so old saved positions cannot be reused.

## Validation
- Native tests: two-contact state machine, clear-stall requirement, no-contact/timeout/cancel paths, settings migration/persistence, both travel bounds and queued-pulse reservations.
- Dashboard tests: sensitivity commands, single/XY homing, sequential execution, cancellation, connection/power failures.
- Existing native/dashboard suites and 45 Python tests pass. Local ARM builds pass for all three board profiles.
- Physical end-stop homing has not been run: mechanism suitability is awaiting operator confirmation. These are inferred commanded-step bounds, not encoder-backed travel protection.

title: Honor stall beeping for uncertain high scores
description: Changes stall beeping behavior to activate for high scores (65) even when confidence is uncertain, while maintaining auto-stop requirements for definite detections.
body:
A high stall-pattern score previously stayed silent whenever the estimator labeled confidence `uncertain`, despite the user enabling stall beeping. Separate audible warnings from the definite-detection timer: fresh valid scores >=65 now beep regardless of confidence, while auto-stop still requires a continuous definite detection and remains off by default.

Expose `stall_beep_active` in telemetry and explain the separate policies in the UI. Use the post-analysis time for freshness checks. Bump firmware to 1.0.15.

Validation: native host suite covers uncertain high-score beeping, low-score/stale suppression, beep-off, and no auto-stop for uncertain warnings. Dashboard suite passes; NEMA17 ARM build passes. CI builds all three boards.

title: Add stall beeping and optional timed auto-stop
description: Changes Add persistent Stall beeping on and Stall time until auto stop settings to the controller and all motor-control pages. Beeping defaults on; auto-stop defaults off (0 seconds). A detected stall produces three rapid 1800 Hz chirps, distinct from the higher-pitched overheat alarm, which retains priority. A configured timeout stops only after a continuous valid stall detection. Free, uncertain, stale, stopped, and unknown states reset the timer. NEMA17 uses its experimental current estimator and NEMA23 uses valid torque stall detection; unsupported DRV8847 boards do not expose the controls. Existing temperature and USB-name settings migrate without being reset.  Validation Native host suite including protocol validation, actual stop behavior, alarm priority, settings migrationpersistence, timeout reset, disabled timeout, and chirp cadence. All dashboard tests and 45 Python tests pass. RP2040 builds for all three board profiles. The NEMA17 detector remains experimental; timing follows its reported stall state and does not supply independent shaft feedback.
body:
## Changes
Add persistent **Stall beeping on** and **Stall time until auto stop** settings to the controller and all motor-control pages. Beeping defaults on; auto-stop defaults off (`0` seconds). A detected stall produces three rapid 1800 Hz chirps, distinct from the higher-pitched overheat alarm, which retains priority.

A configured timeout stops only after a continuous valid stall detection. Free, uncertain, stale, stopped, and unknown states reset the timer. NEMA17 uses its experimental current estimator and NEMA23 uses valid torque stall detection; unsupported DRV8847 boards do not expose the controls. Existing temperature and USB-name settings migrate without being reset.

## Validation
- Native host suite including protocol validation, actual stop behavior, alarm priority, settings migration/persistence, timeout reset, disabled timeout, and chirp cadence.
- All dashboard tests and 45 Python tests pass.
- RP2040 builds for all three board profiles.

The NEMA17 detector remains experimental; timing follows its reported stall state and does not supply independent shaft feedback.

title: Integrate trained speed-conditioned NEMA17 stall estimator
description: The earlier NEMA17 current-pattern indicator used one 500 ms harmonic model and often missed fixture-confirmed stalls at other speeds. Replace it with a speed-conditioned, six-feature model trained from 24 user-labelled recordings. Feature windows are 100 ms at 60100 full stepssec, 400 ms at 25, and 800 ms at 12.5. Thresholds reject the free-running envelope instead of using a class midpoint. Expose explicit freesuspecteduncertain states, keep the unreliable low-speed profile uncertain, and flag interpolation, unfamiliar current patterns and temperatures outside the recorded range. Unsupported speedsvoltage requests return unknown. This remains observational and never controls motion or power. Evaluate every 50 ms and emit lightweight motion telemetry every 100 ms. Trainingexport tools, dataset fingerprint and nested whole-trial validation results are checked in. Retrospective outer-fold worst window error was 61.5, 10, 0, and 8.6 at 12.52560100 respectively; these are small-data development estimates, not universal accuracy claims or a new blind test. Validation: native tests replay eight recorded waveform windows and verify featurescore parity, timing, uncertaintydomain gates, gaps and trace retention; host comparison matches all 24 final-model cases. Dashboard tests and all 45 Python tests pass. RP2040 build succeeds. Firmware 1.0.13 was flashed and re-identified on the target NEMA17; bounded commanded-motion checks verify pulse counts and no dropped samples. A fresh fixture-confirmed stall validation is still needed beyond the recorded data.
body:
The earlier NEMA17 current-pattern indicator used one 500 ms harmonic model and often missed fixture-confirmed stalls at other speeds. Replace it with a speed-conditioned, six-feature model trained from 24 user-labelled recordings. Feature windows are 100 ms at 60/100 full steps/sec, 400 ms at 25, and 800 ms at 12.5. Thresholds reject the free-running envelope instead of using a class midpoint.

Expose explicit free/suspected/uncertain states, keep the unreliable low-speed profile uncertain, and flag interpolation, unfamiliar current patterns and temperatures outside the recorded range. Unsupported speeds/voltage requests return unknown. This remains observational and never controls motion or power. Evaluate every 50 ms and emit lightweight motion telemetry every 100 ms.

Training/export tools, dataset fingerprint and nested whole-trial validation results are checked in. Retrospective outer-fold worst window error was 61.5%, 10%, 0%, and 8.6% at 12.5/25/60/100 respectively; these are small-data development estimates, not universal accuracy claims or a new blind test.

Validation: native tests replay eight recorded waveform windows and verify feature/score parity, timing, uncertainty/domain gates, gaps and trace retention; host comparison matches all 24 final-model cases. Dashboard tests and all 45 Python tests pass. RP2040 build succeeds. Firmware 1.0.13 was flashed and re-identified on the target NEMA17; bounded commanded-motion checks verify pulse counts and no dropped samples. A fresh fixture-confirmed stall validation is still needed beyond the recorded data.

title: Record full-resolution NEMA17 stall transitions after motion stops
description: Adds an opt-in NEMA17 diagnostic recorder for investigating stall-detection latency, retaining the final 4.096 seconds of contiguous 1 kHz current features when deceleration begins, and downloading paged samples only while stopped.
body:
Adds an opt-in NEMA17 diagnostic recorder for investigating stall-detection latency. It retains the final 4.096 seconds of contiguous 1 kHz current features when deceleration begins, then downloads paged samples only while stopped. This avoids USB waveform-export load during the experiment and allocates no additional sample buffer. A device timestamp supports alignment with host-side fixture cues.

The existing detector, its calibration, and motion/fault policies are unchanged. Recording commands do not start motion. Version 1.0.12 exposes the recording protocol.

Validation: native tests cover retention through deceleration, stopped-only reads, ring wrapping, and replacement on the next run; all dashboard tests and 45 Python tests pass; CI builds all three boards successfully. The installed DRV8825 firmware produced a 4,096-bin continuous physical recording with zero dropped samples; repeated recordings in a multi-speed study confirm retention and audio-cue alignment. No claim of improved stall-detection accuracy or speed is made by this change.

title: Move NEMA17 current stall estimator into firmware
description: Move the NEMA17 current-pattern estimator into firmware so USB drops no longer determine its input. Consume the 100 kHz-per-winding ADC stream with an independent cursor, extract 1 kHz waveform features in bounded chunks, and report score, extrapolation status, sample losses, raw ripple RMS and processing time. No estimator result controls motion or power. Normalize logical step modes to physical full-step frequency. Other voltage requests, directions, speeds and temperature conditions produce explicitly unvalidated extrapolations; missing current, faults, insufficient cycles or bandwidth report unknown. The supported feature range is 4320 full stepssec. The dashboard prefers firmware scores and retains the browser estimator for older firmware. Waveform export is now opt-in for this target; default USB traffic contains scores and ordinary telemetry. Optional export uses peak-preserving 10 ms summaries. Firmware 1.0.11. Validation: recorded freestalled waveform tests; logical-resolution, gap, stoppedfault and extrapolation tests; dashboard and Python suites; native firmware builds. Connected-board tests covered all five logical step modes, reverse direction, alternative voltage requests and low speed. Final default-mode runs at 60 and 4 full stepssec analyzed approximately 100,000 samplessec, reported no analysis drops or pulse underruns, and completed commanded pulse counts. Optional waveform export can reduce availability of long uninterrupted windows; 15 V requested produced insufficient winding current to estimate on this setup.
body:
Move the NEMA17 current-pattern estimator into firmware so USB drops no longer determine its input. Consume the 100 kHz-per-winding ADC stream with an independent cursor, extract 1 kHz waveform features in bounded chunks, and report score, extrapolation status, sample losses, raw ripple RMS and processing time. No estimator result controls motion or power.

Normalize logical step modes to physical full-step frequency. Other voltage requests, directions, speeds and temperature conditions produce explicitly unvalidated extrapolations; missing current, faults, insufficient cycles or bandwidth report unknown. The supported feature range is 4–320 full steps/sec. The dashboard prefers firmware scores and retains the browser estimator for older firmware.

Waveform export is now opt-in for this target; default USB traffic contains scores and ordinary telemetry. Optional export uses peak-preserving 10 ms summaries. Firmware 1.0.11.

Validation: recorded free/stalled waveform tests; logical-resolution, gap, stopped/fault and extrapolation tests; dashboard and Python suites; native firmware builds. Connected-board tests covered all five logical step modes, reverse direction, alternative voltage requests and low speed. Final default-mode runs at 60 and 4 full steps/sec analyzed approximately 100,000 samples/sec, reported no analysis drops or pulse underruns, and completed commanded pulse counts. Optional waveform export can reduce availability of long uninterrupted windows; 15 V requested produced insufficient winding current to estimate on this setup.

title: Add experimental NEMA17 current-based stall indicator
description: Add an experimental, observational current-based stall-pattern indicator for the connected DRV8825 NEMA17 motor. It compares 500 ms waveform features with user-confirmed free-running and restrained recordings, displays a 0100 similarity trace, and returns unknown outside the calibrated controller9 V60 full-steps-per-secondforward conditions or when telemetry is unsuitable. It never issues motor or power commands. Fit on two complete runs per class and evaluated on one separate run per class. All ten windows from the two held-out runs separated at the selected threshold; this is a limited experiment, not a calibrated probability or general stall detector. Document the untested conditions and preserve the hardware torque-count limitation. Validation: recorded-waveform feature parity and held-out classification tests, data-coverage and telemetry-state gates, existing dashboard tests, and Python tests. No firmware change.
body:
Add an experimental, observational current-based stall-pattern indicator for the connected DRV8825 NEMA17 motor. It compares 500 ms waveform features with user-confirmed free-running and restrained recordings, displays a 0–100 similarity trace, and returns unknown outside the calibrated controller/9 V/60 full-steps-per-second/forward conditions or when telemetry is unsuitable. It never issues motor or power commands.

Fit on two complete runs per class and evaluated on one separate run per class. All ten windows from the two held-out runs separated at the selected threshold; this is a limited experiment, not a calibrated probability or general stall detector. Document the untested conditions and preserve the hardware torque-count limitation.

Validation: recorded-waveform feature parity and held-out classification tests, data-coverage and telemetry-state gates, existing dashboard tests, and Python tests. No firmware change.

title: Show NEMA17 torque-count and stall-detection support
description: Adds explicit reporting for NEMA17 torque-count and sensorless stall-detection capabilities, displaying null values for unavailable stall data and clarifying hardware limitations in telemetry.
body:
The DRV8825 NEMA17 reports current and temperature but has no torque-count or sensorless stall-detection register. Advertise that capability explicitly, report unavailable stall values as null, and show the hardware limitation alongside the shared current/temperature charts instead of implying a torque trace is merely awaiting data. DRV8452 torque-count reporting stays supported.

Release firmware 1.0.10. Native protocol tests cover unsupported capabilities/null telemetry; dashboard tests cover the explanatory message, hidden torque trace, preserved current trace, and reset behavior.

title: Remove fixed NEMA23 power waits
description: Removes fixed 12-second discharge cooldown and 2-second settling pause for NEMA23 voltage requests, allowing immediate enabling after command success.
body:
NEMA23 voltage requests and power re-enabling no longer impose the fixed 12-second discharge cooldown or 2-second settling pause. Apply the PD request on the next service cycle and permit enabling immediately after the command succeeds. Keep driver wake/SPI timings, fault reporting, and the existing startup failure timeout.

Release firmware 1.0.9 and update dashboard status wording. Verified native tests (including immediate rearm and voltage-request handling), dashboard tests, all 45 Python tests, and the NEMA23 firmware build.

title: Remove discharge wait for NEMA23 current-limit changes
description: Changes the peak winding-current limit on an armed, stopped NEMA23 controller to keep the unchanged supply on while sleeping the driver, allowing verification of the new current setting without a 12-second discharge wait.
body:
Changing the peak winding-current limit on an armed, stopped NEMA23 controller previously switched off the motor supply and started a 12-second discharge wait. Keep the unchanged supply on while sleeping the driver, then verify the new current setting on the next explicit enable without that wait. Existing discharge timers and pending voltage negotiations remain intact.

Release firmware 1.0.8. Verified native tests, dashboard tests, all 45 Python tests, and the NEMA23 firmware build. Regression tests cover immediate rearming, the programmed current DAC, invalid values, and preserving voltage-change waits.

title: Fix motor power rearm countdown and pending enable state
description: Fixes the issue where changing current or power settings could incorrectly report Ready to arm while the firmware still required a discharge wait, leading to a pending enable state after armed telemetry arrived.
body:
Changing current or power settings could report “Ready to arm” while the firmware still required a discharge wait. The dashboard surfaced the rejection instead of waiting, and an enable request could stay marked pending after armed telemetry arrived.

Report the remaining cooldown from firmware, show the real waiting state, start the timer only when motor power actually transitions off, and queue one requested enable until the wait ends. Armed telemetry clears pending UI state. Disconnect, power-off and settings changes cancel pending enable requests. Keep explicit voltage-change discharge/settling behavior and support older firmware's wait response.

Validation: native cooldown and repeated-off-setting regression; dashboard countdown, single retry, already-armed and disconnect cancellation regressions; firmware version tests; local NEMA23 build. Firmware 1.0.7.

Connected-controller check passed on firmware 1.0.7: after power-off, remaining cooldown decreased from 11,994 ms to 9,694 ms and then 9,621 ms while current/override settings were reapplied, rather than restarting. Explicit rearm succeeded at zero with the user's 2 A current setting. No motion commands or step pulses were generated.

title: Report NEMA23 stalls and faults by default; make stopping optional
description: NEMA23 runtime interlock and driver reports previously latched off firmware and independently stopped browser jogging. Add a report-only default and an explicit Stop on detected stall  electrical fault checkbox, off after reboot. Both firmware and browser honor the policy. Hardware interlocks and driver protection still act independently; the UI warns when shaft motion is inhibited and labels positions as commanded. Observe the DRV8452 sensorless torque counter by default, with a configurable software threshold, startupsteady-motion warmup, invalid-data exclusion and 200 ms persistence. Stall indication does not drive nFAULT and causes no software stop unless the optional policy is enabled. Show stall suspected as an uncalibrated indication, with unknown states for shortstoppedstartupfault conditions. Add a torque-count plot sharing the currenttemperature time window. Thermal, sensor, communication and SPI configuration shutdown behavior remains independent. Validation: native defaultopt-in policy, stall debouncerecoveryinvalid-data and protection regressions; all dashboard tests including browser policy, stall controls and chart gaps; 45 Python tests; local NEMA23 UF2 build. Physical shaft-stall accuracy is not yet calibrated. Firmware version: 1.0.6. Connected-board verification: report-only full-scaleinterlock test completed all 160 commanded pulses while recording hardware inhibition, with no firmware latch. The same interlock test with stopping enabled latched off after 49 pulses. At 1 A, forwardreverse commands completed 640 pulses each, and a longer run yielded live torque counts of 1226. FNB58 input-voltagecurrent packets were CRC-validated throughout. These are commandsensor checks, not calibrated physical stall detection. The live stall-notification path was also checked with a deliberately high temporary threshold (4095), without inducing a physical shaft stall: reporting-only emitted stall suspected and completed all 1280 requested pulses; opt-in stopping latched on the indication after 608 pulses. Threshold 3, stop mode off, the users 3 A setting and disabled motor power were restored afterward. This validates notificationpolicy integration, not physical-stall classification accuracy.
body:
NEMA23 runtime interlock and driver reports previously latched off firmware and independently stopped browser jogging. Add a report-only default and an explicit “Stop on detected stall / electrical fault” checkbox, off after reboot. Both firmware and browser honor the policy. Hardware interlocks and driver protection still act independently; the UI warns when shaft motion is inhibited and labels positions as commanded.

Observe the DRV8452 sensorless torque counter by default, with a configurable software threshold, startup/steady-motion warmup, invalid-data exclusion and 200 ms persistence. Stall indication does not drive nFAULT and causes no software stop unless the optional policy is enabled. Show “stall suspected” as an uncalibrated indication, with unknown states for short/stopped/startup/fault conditions. Add a torque-count plot sharing the current/temperature time window. Thermal, sensor, communication and SPI configuration shutdown behavior remains independent.

Validation: native default/opt-in policy, stall debounce/recovery/invalid-data and protection regressions; all dashboard tests including browser policy, stall controls and chart gaps; 45 Python tests; local NEMA23 UF2 build. Physical shaft-stall accuracy is not yet calibrated. Firmware version: 1.0.6.

Connected-board verification: report-only full-scale/interlock test completed all 160 commanded pulses while recording hardware inhibition, with no firmware latch. The same interlock test with stopping enabled latched off after 49 pulses. At 1 A, forward/reverse commands completed 640 pulses each, and a longer run yielded live torque counts of 12–26. FNB58 input-voltage/current packets were CRC-validated throughout. These are command/sensor checks, not calibrated physical stall detection.

The live stall-notification path was also checked with a deliberately high temporary threshold (4095), without inducing a physical shaft stall: reporting-only emitted “stall suspected” and completed all 1280 requested pulses; opt-in stopping latched on the indication after 608 pulses. Threshold 3, stop mode off, the user's 3 A setting and disabled motor power were restored afterward. This validates notification/policy integration, not physical-stall classification accuracy.

title: Retain NEMA23 fault cause before isolating power
description: Preserves GPIO levels and driver fault register before isolating power, reporting separate interlock-loss and driver-fault messages for NEMA23.
body:
NEMA23 faults previously collapsed driver nFAULT and the shared power/temperature interlock into one message, then isolated power before the original input levels could be inspected. Preserve GPIO levels and, when readable, the driver fault register before isolation, and report separate GPIO24 interlock-loss and GPIO23 driver-fault messages. Firmware version is 1.0.5.

Validation: native regression tests verify the retained driver and interlock snapshots, all dashboard tests and 45 Python tests pass, NEMA23 UF2 builds locally. On the connected controller, a bounded full-scale test reproduced a GPIO24 interlock drop after 51 pulses with the driver fault register clear; the same requested 20 V test at 1 A completed all 160 pulses without a fault. This establishes the signal and current-setting dependency, not a measured supply-voltage diagnosis.

At requested 20 V and 1 A, two further finite moves at the dashboard speed of 150 half-steps/sec completed 20 half steps forward and reverse, exactly 160 hardware pulses per direction with no fault. Final controller state is 1 A, configured winding limit enabled, stopped and power disarmed. Shaft motion was not independently observed by the agent.

title: Add independent NEMA23 current-protection overrides
description: Adds two separate NEMA23 dashboard checkboxes: Ignore overcurrent fault shutdown selects DRV8452 OCP auto-retry and bypasses only OCP-only software shutdown; Disable peak winding-current limit uses the boards approximately 3.965 A peak full-scale setting while retaining the configured cap for restoration.
body:
Adds two separate NEMA23 dashboard checkboxes: “Ignore overcurrent fault shutdown” selects DRV8452 OCP auto-retry and bypasses only OCP-only software shutdown; “Disable peak winding-current limit” uses the board’s approximately 3.965 A peak full-scale setting while retaining the configured cap for restoration.

Both overrides default off on reboot, require a stopped motor, and disconnect motor power when changed. Hardware OCP remains active; mixed/unknown faults, SPI failures, thermal foldback and thermal shutdown remain enforced. Raw fault telemetry stays visible. Firmware version is 1.0.4 and controls are capability-gated for older devices.

Validation: native firmware suite including independent-mode, fault classification and foldback regressions; all dashboard tests; 45 Python tests; local NEMA23 UF2 build.

title: Remove NEMA23 PD negotiation gate and extend test tone
description: Removes PD negotiation verification for NEMA23 power gating and extends test tone duration to two seconds with an optional parameter.
body:
NEMA23 power could remain blocked by “PD negotiation was not verified” even though the board has no voltage measurement path. Remove contract-status/current and PG-transition verification from power gating. Send an acknowledged fixed-voltage request, wait two seconds, then permit explicit arming; best-effort PD register readings are informational and cannot latch off power. Keep write failures distinguishable from unverified voltage, preserve the discharge interval and the existing optional raw-PG override.

Change the dashboard settling text and label PD-reported current as informational. Extend Test tone to two seconds through a bounded optional `duration_ms` command parameter; older callers retain the 600 ms default. Tone acceptance and PWM telemetry are not proof of audible sound.

Version firmware and dashboard minimum as 1.0.3.

Validation: native regression tests cover settling without PG transitions or readable PD status, low current/status readings during arm, loss of status reads while armed, finite two-second test tones and invalid durations. Native motion/settings/current/board suites, dashboard, single-motor, gantry, positions, firmware status and 45 Python tests pass. NEMA23 UF2 builds successfully. Existing controller 1.0.2 accepted a beep and reported PWM changing from off to 2731 Hz; acoustic output remains unconfirmed.

Buzzer diagnostics: initialize the PWM pin and counter for each tone and sample GPIO3 for 1 ms during an explicit beep. Expose pin function, before/after PWM counters and low/high observations as diagnostic telemetry. On the connected controller, the counter advances and pin function is PWM, but GPIO3 readback stays low; the user confirmed the short tone was silent. The acoustic/output-path issue is unresolved and is not claimed fixed.

Installed final firmware 1.0.3 (build be73e5918667e7e6). A 15 V request reaches Ready to arm without the removed negotiation verification. Previous PG and fuse-fault override preferences are restored; motor power is left disarmed. No movement commands were sent.

title: Add optional fuse power fault override for NEMA23
description: Adds an optional checkbox to ignore fuse power fault input for NEMA23 controllers, allowing operation even when a fault is asserted, while maintaining safety checks and telemetry visibility.
body:
NEMA23 controllers can report the eFuse fault input as asserted even when a meter reads the expected supply. Add an optional **Ignore fuse power fault** checkbox that bypasses GPIO2 fault-input gating while keeping the raw signal visible.

The option defaults off, resets on reboot, accepts only a boolean while stopped, and disarms power whenever changed. The checkbox cancels queued enable requests and never arms power or starts motion. Protected-rail power-good, PD contract/current, temperature, driver/SPI, USB and heartbeat checks remain active, as do the eFuse hardware protections. Older firmware hides the unsupported checkbox.

Bump native firmware and the dashboard minimum version to 1.0.2.

Validation: native tests cover default/reset behavior, malformed requests, low fault input with and without override, raw telemetry, moving rejection, explicit disarm, rail timeout/interlock and thermal shutdown; board-control tests cover capability visibility, command fields, no automatic arm, checked state and moving interlock. Dashboard, firmware-version, single-motor, gantry, saved-position and DRV8847 dashboard suites and 45 Python tests pass. Native NEMA23 UF2 builds successfully.

Hardware integration: flashed version 1.0.2 (build c3209be4ba730907) onto controller e6658c344b0a562a and verified override true/false telemetry while the raw fault input stayed asserted. Both changes left motor power disarmed with zero step pulses. Final override is off. No arming or physical motion test was performed.

title: Fix missing polygon-pad plated holes
description: Fixes rendering issues with polygon-pad plated holes by translating pad outlines into board coordinates and reusing existing copper, soldermask, and drill passes, ensuring drill offsets are maintained correctly.
body:
Polygon-pad plated holes currently disappear with an unsupported-shape diagnostic. Translate the already-oriented pad outline into board coordinates and reuse the existing copper, soldermask, and drill passes, keeping drill offsets in board coordinates. Three separate regression tests cover all drill shapes, offsets, layers, mask openings, exact concave boundaries, and pad orientation against the pinned reference renderer; update the five affected snapshots. No new defaults, dependencies, or reference-renderer patches are introduced.

Motivation: Render polygon-pad plated holes without losing their copper and drill or forcing diagnostic-aware viewers to fall back.
